**Answer: no, the first wave can't start.** The preflight check (`check_orchestration.py preflight`) has not run. I have no shell in this session, so I can't run it and I'm not giving a checker verdict. I read the plan, the preflight record, the profile and `autonomy-preflight.md` by hand instead. The checker would reject this record on at least six points, so the run would stop before it started.

**What I found**

The plan was checked for an attended run, not an unattended one. The preflight record doesn't match tonight's window or this plan, and it gives one test account to two packages that run at the same time. The first wave starts only when the preflight check returns `PASS`.

| # | Defect | Where | Expected code |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| 1 | The plan doesn't have `execution.unattended: true`, and P1–P3 don't list their `needs`. P1 and P2 run commands to pass their acceptance criteria, so each must at least list an `environment` need. | `plan.json:15-22`, every package | `NEEDS_UNDECLARED` |
| 2 | The record never says which plan revision it was made for: there is no `plan.digest` or `plan.base` field. Fixing #1 changes the plan, which changes its digest, so this has to be written after #1. | `preflight.json` | `PREFLIGHT_STALE` |
| 3 | The window in the record is 2026-11-13 22:00Z to 2026-11-14 08:00Z, which is three days ago. Tonight is 2026-11-16 22:00 to 2026-11-17 08:00. The times are in UTC, so check they match the lead's local 22:00. | `preflight.json:3-6` | stale window |
| 4 | `REPO_TOKEN` expires 2026-11-14T03:00Z. That was before the end of the old window and is already past now. | `preflight.json:62` | `CREDENTIAL_EXPIRES` |
| 5 | U1 (clerk-a) is assigned to both P1 and P2. They run together in wave 1, and U1 can write, not just read. Probe E4 already logs in as clerk-b, but no account entry gives clerk-b to P2. | `preflight.json:80-92` | `ACCOUNT_CONFLICT` |
| 6 | No entry in the record has `covers`, so even after #1, every declared need is uncovered. | access, accounts, environment entries | `PREREQUISITE_UNCOVERED` |

These parts already meet the rules: the baseline `npm test` (E6) passed at base `3f9c2e1`, and all probes ran on that commit. Both increments are ready (I2 is partly ready but reversible). D1 is answered. D2 is a reversible default, so it will wait for the human to confirm at merge. The escalation channel was tested (E7). The read-only auditor U3 is shared correctly. There are no secret values in the record, and no human step falls during the window.

**Why it matters**

Started as it is, the run would fail in two ways. The gate rejects an unattended run without a passing preflight, so none of the night's work could reach the merge boundary. And P1 and P2 sharing clerk-a can corrupt each other's test data. Each defect has a clear fix.

**Do this first**

1. Fix the plan in `.alchemy/runs/r1/plan.json`:
   - Set `execution.unattended: true`.
   - Add `needs` to P1, P2 and P3, covering the repository, the build environment, the clerk-a/clerk-b accounts and the auditor account.
   - Re-run `python .claude/skills/alchemy-orchestrate/scripts/check_orchestration.py plan .alchemy/runs/r1/plan.json --profile alchemy-workspace.json --root .` and note the `plan_digest` it prints.
2. Rewrite the preflight record:
   - Add `plan: {digest, base: "3f9c2e1"}`.
   - Set the window to 2026-11-16T22:00/2026-11-17T08:00 in the lead's zone.
   - Issue a new `REPO_TOKEN` that expires after the window ends, and re-probe it.
   - Add a clerk-b account for P2 only, with its own reset command, and change U1 to P1 only.
   - Add `covers` to every entry.
   - Run the new token's probe at `3f9c2e1`. The other probes can be carried over because the base hasn't moved.
3. Run `check_orchestration.py preflight .alchemy/runs/r1/preflight.json --plan .alchemy/runs/r1/plan.json --profile alchemy-workspace.json --root .`. Start wave 1 (P1 and P2) only if it returns `PASS`.

**What I did not check**

- **Plan check:** I didn't re-run it, so I'm relying on your statement that it passed. Step 1 above re-runs it.
- **Preflight check:** not run. Step 3 above runs it.
- **Probe E4:** I couldn't confirm it proves the auditor's read-only role rather than just a login. That needs a look at what `npm run probe:login` asserts.
- **Plan approval:** the record lists "approve the plan" as a step before the window, but nothing shows it was done. The lead or another human needs to confirm it.
- **Cloud access:** the plan doesn't show whether any package actually needs A2 (the test cloud). That gets settled when the `needs` are written.
- **Host:** whether the machine stays awake and the runtime stays open for the whole window is for the lead to confirm before 22:00.
